title: Square roots and completing the square

learn.title: Undoing a square
learn.body: If $x^2=k$, then $x=\pm\sqrt{k}$. There are two answers because $4^2$ and $(-4)^2$ both equal 16. This also works when a whole bracket is squared: $(x-1)^2=9$ gives $x-1=\pm3$.

learn.title: Solve $(x-1)^2=9$
learn.body: Take the square root of both sides.

learn.title: Completing the square
learn.body: To turn $x^2+bx$ into a perfect square, add $\left(\frac{b}{2}\right)^2$. For $x^2+6x$ add 9, since $x^2+6x+9=(x+3)^2$. Add the same number to both sides.

learn.title: Solve $x^2+6x+5=0$
learn.body: Move the constant, then complete the square.
Whatever you add to complete the square, add to both sides. Otherwise the equation changes.
